World-map artifact list: native source grammar, Windows 53.16

Source images are data/runtime/native-pe-images.json reference and classic.
This document reconstructs the text-producing control flow from the two local
PE images. list-native-*.asm contains complete source spans; list-branches.tsv,
list-calls.tsv and list-switches.tsv retain instruction addresses, arguments,
conditions, and decoded tables. Jump-table data is excluded from disassembly.

ARTIFACT LIST OWNER
Steam world renderer: 0x1401c17e0..0x1401d3abc.
Steam artifact tab: 0x1401d1a1b..0x1401d22b5.
Classic world renderer: 0x1401c1770..0x1401d3a4c.
Classic artifact tab: 0x1401d19ab..0x1401d2245.
The screen holds artifact pointers at +0x8410, parallel location-cache pointers
at +0x8428, scroll at +0x8440, and hovered artifact at +0x8448. It renders each
artifact as a three-row skin with two textual rows. Cache construction occurs
only when the parallel pointer is null; hover construction is a different call
(Steam 0x1401d9c30, Classic 0x1401d9bc0).

TITLE ROW
Steam 0x1401d1de2 calls 0x140b94400 with artifact.id and flags=0.
Classic 0x1401d1d72 calls 0x140b91440 with the same arguments.
The shared formatter resolves the artifact id, then formats artifact.name at
record+0x8 through the English language-name formatter. If the resulting name
is nonempty, use it. If empty, inspect item through vtable+0x0 (type), and
vtable+0xe0 with flag 0x14 (written item). Type 0x59, type 0x57, or flag 0x14
produces the inline literal "Untitled". Other empty names call the item identity
formatter (Steam 0x140c65450) with include_quality=true. An unresolved artifact
id produces "an unknown artifact". LPAGE:ARTIFACT/BOOK wrappers in the shared
formatter are unreachable here because its caller passes flags=0.
The ordinary item subgrammar is separately sourced in
data/extracted/item-description-sources.tsv; it is not a list-specific literal.

STATUS ROW: STRICT PRIORITY
The following conditions are tested in order, not combined as independent text.

1. cache+0x10 holder_hf != -1
   Steam condition 0x1401d1e95, text 0x1401d1ea0, call 0x1401d1ee7.
   "Last held by " + historical_figure_name(holder_hf).
   Shared Steam formatter 0x140b92f10; Classic 0x140b8ff50.
   A freshly initialized context is passed, fifth argument=1, sixth argument=0.
   Named holder: when the descriptor is enabled, print "the " + optional
   "zombie " + optional "ghostly " + caste/creature singular + optional raw
   transformed-form label + " " before the English name. When the descriptor
   is disabled, print only the English name. The sixth argument is 0, so the
   sixth=2 suffix " the {creature}" is not enabled for artifact holders.
   Unnamed holder: print "a " + optional zombie/ghostly + creature/caste
   descriptor + optional transformed-form label. Unresolved figure id yields
   "an unknown creature". A named holder can produce an empty suffix if the
   descriptor is disabled and the English name is empty. For example race=-1
   disables descriptor at 0x140b931fa..0x140b93207; name.has_name=true reaches
   0x140b934ec..0x140b93504; sixth=0 omits the optional suffix after that call.
   Thus the native list can emit bare "Last held by ".
   The fresh context constructor (Steam 0x140072080, Classic 0x140072010)
   installs current_hf=-1. Therefore the unnamed actor's alternate "the "
   branch is unreachable for a resolved nonnegative figure id in this list.
   Unnamed creature formatter (Steam 0x140aa3bd0..0x140aa3d93; Classic
   0x140aa0c50..0x140aa0e13) receives plural=false. Invalid/out-of-range caste
   falls back to valid creature.name[0]; invalid/out-of-range race contributes
   no creature text, with no unknown placeholder. The named descriptor uses
   the same singular raw selection inline at 0x140b933a6..0x140b93472.
   If creature text is empty, the unnamed suffix can be "a", "a zombie",
   "a ghostly", or "a zombie ghostly" after trimming. If a named holder's
   descriptor remains enabled (e.g. nonnegative out-of-range race), and name
   is also empty, its suffix can be "the", "the zombie", "the ghostly", or
   "the zombie ghostly". The zombie/ghostly branches are independent, with
   no native mutual-exclusion branch. Each can also contain the raw transformed
   creature label at unit+0x90 when unit+0x88 is set; this flag suppresses
   ghostly, so transformed suffixes have no ghostly component. If that raw
   label is empty, the same closed suffixes above remain possible.
   Conversation-only interrogator/subject and LPAGE
   paths visible in the shared function are not enabled by this caller.

2. cache+0x8 storage_site != -1
   Steam condition 0x1401d1f91, text 0x1401d1f9c, call 0x1401d1fc5.
   "Last in " + site_name(storage_site), flags=0.
   Shared Steam formatter 0x140b93930; Classic 0x140b90970.
   Resolve world_site, format its name at +0x0 via English language-name
   formatter; unresolved id yields "an unknown site". An existing site whose
   name.has_name=false yields empty name, as does a named site whose first
   name, nickname and all valid word forms contribute no text. The shared
   site helper appends that empty result without a fallback, so both produce
   bare "Last in ".
   storage_structure_local (cache+0xc) is not printed in this list status.

3. cache+0x14 loss_region != -1
   Steam condition 0x1401d2075, text 0x1401d2080, call 0x1401d20a9.
   "Last in " + surface_region_name(loss_region), flags=0.
   Shared Steam formatter 0x140b94a40; Classic 0x140b91a80.
   Resolve world_region, format its name at +0x0 via English language-name
   formatter; unresolved id yields "an unknown region". Existing region with
   name.has_name=false or no text-producing name fields yields an empty name
   without fallback, so these also produce bare "Last in ".

4. cache+0x18 last_layer != -1
   Steam condition 0x1401d2159, text 0x1401d2164, call 0x1401d218d.
   "Last in " + underground_region_name(last_layer), flags=0.
   Shared Steam formatter 0x140b94940; Classic 0x140b91980.
   Missing region pointer: "an unknown underground region".
   Existing region with name.has_name at region+0x7a != 0: empty suffix, because
   this native helper skips its generic label and contains no named formatter.
   Unnamed region: type at region+0x0 == 0 -> "the depths of the world";
   type == 1 -> "the magma sea"; type == 2 -> "the Underworld"; other -> empty.
   The native empty result is therefore also a real branch: bare "Last in ".

5. all above fields == -1
   Steam text 0x1401d223a: "Location unknown".
   Classic equivalent text 0x1401d21ca.

Title clipping and each status clipping happen only after the complete field is
constructed. Titles resize to available width minus 3; status fields resize to
width minus 4; sufficiently wide clipped fields have their last three bytes
replaced by '.'. This is a display branch, not a distinct source name.
The source field passed to the native draw call remains a single title/status;
do not identify partial English words as separately owned list columns.

LOCATION CACHE DATAFLOW
Steam seed 0x1409de8e0; Classic seed 0x1409dc110.
artifact+0x108 storage_site -> cache+0x8.
artifact+0x10c storage_structure_local -> cache+0xc.
artifact+0x110 loss_region -> cache+0x14.
artifact+0x114 last_layer -> cache+0x18.
artifact+0x118 holder_hf -> cache+0x10.
artifact+0x11c year -> cache+0x1c.
artifact+0x120 season_tick -> cache+0x20.
cache+0x28 is invalidated to zero by every accepted change.

Steam rumor update 0x1409de930..0x1409dedc9 (code), jump data to 0x1409dee30.
Classic rumor update 0x1409dc160..0x1409dc5f9 (code), jump data to 0x1409dc660.
The seed is followed by local entity rumors at global ui+0x1250.
Rumors flagged at +0x20 bit 0 are skipped; future rumor year/tick is skipped;
older observation year/tick than cache year/tick is skipped. Artifact id must
match. The dispatch range is rumor.type 2..33; other values are skipped.

Type 2 incident: resolve incident by id; require incident.type=7 and matching
artifact id. Its location state 0 Held, 2 Gained, 4 Denied installs hf.hfid as
holder and clears site/region/layer. State 3 Given installs second_hf.hfid as
holder and clears site/region/layer. State 1 Dropped installs site_id/site_bld,
subregion/layer, then clears holder. State 5 Destroyed clears site/region/layer
and holder. Out-of-range incident states update only observation timestamp.
Type 25 artifact_in_site: sets site and structure, clears region/layer/holder.
Type 26 artifact_in_subregion: sets region, clears site/structure/layer/holder.
Type 27 artifact_in_feature_layer: sets layer, clears site/structure/region/holder.
Type 28 artifact_in_inventory: sets holder, clears site/structure/region/layer.
Type 29 artifact_not_in_site: only accepts matching current site, and matching
structure when rumor structure != -1; clears site/structure only.
Type 30 artifact_not_in_subregion: only accepts matching region; clears it only.
Type 31 artifact_not_in_feature_layer: only accepts matching layer; clears it only.
Type 32 artifact_not_in_inventory: only accepts matching holder; clears it only.
Type 33 artifact_was_destroyed: clears site/structure/region/layer/holder.
Types 3..24 and types outside 2..33: no cache update or output.
All accepted cases save observation year/tick and invalidate cache+0x28.
None of these cases directly prints extra list text; they feed the five-way
priority grammar above.

GENERATED NAMES AND WORD FORMS
Steam English formatter 0x140a946e0..0x140a94ea2.
Classic English formatter 0x140a91760..0x140a91f22.
Site and surface-region calls pass capitalize=true, short=false.
The language_name contains first_name+0x0, nickname+0x20, words+0x40 (7 ids),
parts_of_speech+0x5c (7 int16), and has_name+0x72. has_name=false produces no
name. Nickname output depends on the native nickname setting; quotes are '`'
and '\''. The complete grammar then considers these slots in native order:
words[0]+words[1] front/rear compound; words[2] first adjective;
words[3] second adjective; words[4] hyphen compound, followed by '-';
words[5] noun; words[6] Of phrase. Slots whose id is -1 are absent. Optional
first name/nickname and prior components are separated by spaces. A The/the
prefix is inserted before the first present adjective/hyphen/noun component;
Of/of is inserted for the final Of phrase. Each slot uses its own POS value;
the noun is not constrained to singular or inferred from its English spelling.

Steam word-form leaf 0x140d2cb50..0x140d2cc1c (no unwind entry).
Classic word-form leaf 0x140d29b90..0x140d29c5c (no unwind entry).
Invalid word id or POS outside 0..8 contributes no text. The dispatch table
selects word.forms; appended text is the entire form, which can contain spaces.
POS 0 Noun -> word+0x20; 1 NounPlural -> +0x40; 2 Adjective -> +0x60;
3 Prefix -> +0x80; 4 Verb -> +0xa0; 5 Verb3rdPerson -> +0xc0;
6 VerbPast -> +0xe0; 7 VerbPassive -> +0x100; 8 VerbGerund -> +0x120.
The exact state/POS targets for both PEs are in list-switches.tsv.

"The Amazing Fingers" is a generated name in the native site/region role of
the Last in field. The title-shaped The + adjective + plural noun grammar is
native; it is not a squad.alias field. Static PE text cannot reveal the saved
world's particular site-vs-region selector or word ids. Runtime name lexicons
already contain amazing and finger/fingers; translate this generated family
through its typed name grammar rather than add the screenshot's whole name.
Dynamic word strings and custom/modded first names are world raw/save data,
not a finite set of PE literals. Unsupported dynamic strings remain bounded
to the same native field; they do not change the ownership or source type.

SIBLING MISSING-CITIZENS LIST
Steam 0x1401d1062..0x1401d1702; Classic 0x1401d0ff2..0x1401d1692.
This sibling reuses the two-line skin, but the title is historical_figure_name
with fifth=1/sixth=2. No info object or whereabouts pointer yields title only.
Otherwise test whereabouts site(+0x4), surface region(+0x8), underground
layer(+0xc), then army_id(+0x10). The first three produce the same "Last in "
location union. If all absent and army_id!=-1, print "Last known to be traveling";
otherwise print "Location unknown". Traveling is not an artifact-list branch.
